messages:
alex: Quick Q—Java SDK + GCP SA impersonation: after I switch the projectId on the client config, the OIDC token aud still reflects the old project. Anyone seen token caching survive project change?

maria: Hmm, is the SDK caching id tokens keyed by serviceAccountEmail only? That could explain it. Do you have a repro or code snippet?

alex: Yep repro below. Creating ImpersonatedCredentials and reusing the HttpCredentialsAdapter across clients.

alex: ```java
ImpersonatedCredentials creds = ImpersonatedCredentials.create(
    sourceCreds, // user SA
    Arrays.asList("roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"),
    "target-sa@proj-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
    3600);
HttpCredentialsAdapter adapter = new HttpCredentialsAdapter(creds);
// then new MyClient.Builder().setCredentials(adapter).setProjectId("proj-b").build();
```

alex: The token's aud: https://iamcredentials.googleapis.com/projects/proj-a/... even though projectId is proj-b

sam: ah yep, adapter caches AccessToken in creds.getRequestMetadata() and doesn't include projectId in cache key. We saw similar in python a while back.

jia: What if you call creds.refresh() between switches? Also check if target_audience vs scope flow — id tokens use target_audience, access tokens use scopes.

alex: Calling refresh helps but it's racy in our pooled client reuse. I pushed a small change to include projectId in the cached key heuristically. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/sdk-java/pull/402

maria: Can you paste the minimal log showing token value+aud and timestamps?

alex: ```
[2026-02-12T15:04:21Z] INFO TokenManager: cached token for key=target-sa@proj-a|scopes=[...] expiry=2026-02-12T16:04:21Z aud=https://iamcredentials.googleapis.com/... 
[2026-02-12T15:04:45Z] INFO ClientInit: switched project -> proj-b, using existing TokenManager key -> target-sa@proj-a|...
```

sam: Suggestion: instead of changing cache key, treat credentials immutable per client instance. If you need multi-project, create per-project client pools.

alex: Good idea. For our service we need cheap per-request project override though. So I think including projectId in key is ok here.

jia: small nit: ensure you don't accidentally include secrets in cache key logging. Also add unit test for concurrent refresh.

alex: Will do. @maria @sam can one of you take a quick CR? I want to merge today to avoid rollout break. :pray:

maria: I can review in 30m.

sam: I'll take perf + concurrency review.
